                                                             Reset period programming pin. Connecting this pin to VDD through a 40kΩ to 200kΩ

    CT                  4              3           I
                                                             pin to a ground referenced capacitor ≥ 100pF gives a user-programmable delay time. See

    GND                 2              5          —          Ground
                                                             Driving the manual reset pin ( MR) low asserts RESET. MR is internally tied to VDD by a
    MR                  3              4           I
                                                             90kΩ pull-up resistor.
                                                             RESET is an open-drain output that is driven to a low-impedance state when RESET is
                                                             asserted (either the SENSE input is lower than the threshold voltage (VIT) or the MR pin is
    RESET               1              6          O          set to a logic low). RESET remains low (asserted) for the reset period after both SENSE
                                                             is above VIT and MR is set to a logic high. A pull-up resistor from 10kΩ to 1MΩ should be
                                                             used on this pin, and allows the reset pin to attain voltages higher than VDD.
                                                             This pin is connected to the voltage to be monitored. If the voltage at this terminal drops
    SENSE               5              2           I
                                                             below the threshold voltage VIT, then RESET is asserted.
                                                             Supply voltage. It is good analog design practice to place a 0.1μF ceramic capacitor close
